1985.notes: 71st Annual Report of the South Carolina Tax Commission, 1985 (microfilm scan on archive.org), Legislative Summary 1985, House Bill 2640, Section 8 (printed p. 108, read from the page image): for 1985 the personal exemption is indexed from $1,000 to $1,040, the zero bracket amount from $2,300 to $2,390 (single) and $3,400 to $3,540 (joint), and the width of each tax bracket from $2,000 to $2,020, effective January 1, 1985. Federal income tax deductible, limited to $500 (not modelled).

Code 12-7-215, for tax years beginning after 1988) indexes the brackets annually by half the CPI change, limited to 0.5% in 1989, 1% in 1990, 2% in 1991 and 4% after 1991; and the rate on the first $2,000 of taxable income is reduced from 3% to 2.75% only from 1990. 2008.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates as of July 1, 2009, sheet '2009' of the State Individual Income Tax Rates 2000-2014 workbook): South Carolina row prints 0% > $0, 3% > $2,670, 4% > $5,340, 5% > $8,010, 6% > $10,680, 7% > $13,350, and footnote (n) says the Idaho, Montana and South Carolina brackets listed apply to tax year 2008. The Federation of Tax Administrators' table 'for tax year 2008 -- as of January 1, 2008' (https://web.archive.org/web/20080607033003/http://www.taxadmin.org/FTA/rate/ind_inc.html) agrees: rates 0-7.0%, 6 brackets, lowest $2,670, highest $13,350 (intermediate edges not printed there), and SC DOR's 2007-08 annual report reprints the same FTA row. Bottom bracket 0% from 2007 (S.C. Code 12-6-515). Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

Bottom bracket 0% from 2007 (S.C. Code 12-6-515, 2007 Act 115). Bracket edges from SC Board of Economic Advisors TY2009 table (dc.statelibrary.sc.gov item a823afd3); checked against the 2009 SC1040 booklet: rate schedule 7% minus $466 matches, and the tax table is consistent. Two-wage-earner credit not modelled.

Two-wage-earner credit not modelled.

2012.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates as of July 1, 2012, sheet '2012' of the State Individual Income Tax Rates 2000-2014 workbook): South Carolina single and couple schedules print 0% > $0, 3% > $2,800, 4% > $5,600, 5% > $8,400, 6% > $11,200, 7% > $14,000 (sources given as the state form and the 2012 SC1040-ES). FTA's table 'for tax year 2012 -- as of January 1, 2012' (https://web.archive.org/web/20120510161521/http://www.taxadmin.org/fta/rate/ind_inc.pdf) agrees on the range ($2,800-$14,000, 0-7%). Checked against the 2012 SC1040 booklet (https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/SC/2012/IIT_PACKET_WEB_10312012.pdf): rate schedule 7% minus $476 matches, and these brackets reproduce every row of its tax table. Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

2014.notes: Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. TY2014 brackets from the SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office 'State Individual Income Tax Comparisons' presentation to the House Tax Policy Review Committee (Sept. 13, 2016; tax liability calculation table for tax year 2014); consistent with the 2014 SC1040 rate schedule (7% minus $490). 2015.notes: 2015 brackets from the SC Department of Revenue's 2015 SC1040ES estimated-tax worksheet tax computation schedule: $0-2,910 0%, 2,910-5,820 3%, 5,820-8,730 4%, 8,730-11,640 5%, 11,640-14,550 6%, over 14,550 7% less $495. Checked against the 2015 SC1040TT tax table (https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/SC/2015/SC1040TT_06152015.pdf): rate schedule 7% minus $495 matches and these brackets reproduce every row. The Tax Foundation's 2015 table (repeating the 2014 brackets) does not match and was not used. Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

2016.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets for 2016, Fiscal Fact No. 500 data workbook): South Carolina single and joint schedules print 0% > $0, 3% > $2,920, 4% > $5,840, 5% > $8,760, 6% > $11,680, 7% > $14,600. Single source; checked against the 2016 SC1040 booklet (https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/SC/2016/IITPack_2016.pdf): rate schedule 7% minus $496 matches, and these brackets reproduce every row of its tax table (the Tax Foundation's 2015 table, which repeats the 2014 brackets, does not match the 2015 tax table and was not used). Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

2017.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets for 2017, Fiscal Fact No. 544 data workbook, Dec. 2017 update): South Carolina single and joint schedules print 0% > $0, 3% > $2,930, 4% > $5,860, 5% > $8,790, 6% > $11,720, 7% > $14,650; the Tax Foundation's 2018 workbook repeats them on its '2017' sheet. Single source; checked against the 2017 SC1040TT tax table (https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/SC/2017/SC1040TT_2017.pdf): these brackets reproduce every row (33 rows where the exact tax ends in 50 cents are printed rounded down), including $6,498 on $99,900-$100,000; the booklet's rate schedule constant ($499) is $1 more than these brackets give ($498.10). Starts from federal taxable income, so deduction = federal standard deduction + personal exemptions for the year (federal amounts). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

2018.notes: Secondary source (Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets for 2018, Fiscal Fact No. 576 data workbook, '2018' sheet): South Carolina single and joint schedules print 3% > $2,970, 4% > $5,940, 5% > $8,910, 6% > $11,880, 7% > $14,860 (income below $2,970 untaxed, the 0% bracket of S.C. Code 12-6-515). Single source; checked against the 2018 SC1040 booklet (https://taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/SC/2018/IITPacket_2018.pdf): rate schedule 7% minus $505 matches, and these brackets reproduce every row of its tax table (9 rows where the exact tax ends in 50 cents are printed rounded down). Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = federal standard deduction (no federal personal exemption after 2017). Same brackets for all filing statuses. SC dependent exemption, two-wage-earner credit and other SC deductions not modelled.

2019.notes: SC Department of Revenue Form SC4972 (Tax on Lump-Sum Distributions), 2019, '2019 South Carolina Tax Rate Schedule': $0 below $3,030; 3% of the amount less $91 from $3,030; 4% less $152 from $6,060; 5% less $242 from $9,090; 6% less $364 from $12,120; 7% less $515 from $15,160. The constants are consistent with these bracket edges (each equals the tax at the edge under the lower rate, to the dollar). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = the 2019 federal standard deduction ($12,200 single, $24,400 joint), as in this file's 2018 and 2020 entries. SC dependent exemption and other SC deductions not modelled.

2020.notes: Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = federal standard deduction (no federal personal exemption after 2017). Same brackets for all filing statuses. Brackets from SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office (taken from 2020 SC forms); consistent with the 2020 SC1040TT tax table (7% minus $523). SC dependent exemption and other SC deductions not modelled.

2021.notes: Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = federal standard deduction. Same brackets for all filing statuses. Brackets from SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office H.4216 analysis (Tax Year 2021 table); consistent with the 2021 SC1040TT tax table (7% minus $529). SC dependent exemption not modelled.

2022.notes: Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = federal standard deduction. Same brackets for all filing statuses. 2022 Act 228 (S.C. Code 12-6-510(B)) collapsed six brackets to three for TY2022: 0% to $3,200, 3% to $16,040, top rate 6.5% for 2022. DOR's 2022 rate schedule (6.5% minus $658) implies the 6.5% band starts at about $16,057 due to rounding. SC dependent exemption not modelled.

2023.notes: Starts from federal taxable income: deduction = federal standard deduction. Same brackets for all filing statuses. TY2023 brackets from SC Revenue and Fiscal Affairs Office (Sept 2023): 0% to $3,330, 3% to $16,680, 6.4% above. NOTE: the DOR 2023 SC1040TT rate schedule (6.4% minus $670) and tax table imply the 6.4% band starts near $16,770, not $16,680; unresolved. SC dependent exemption not modelled.

2024.notes: Starts from federal taxable income. Bracket edges are derived from the official tax table.

2025.notes: Starts from federal taxable income, but South Carolina conforms to the IRC only as of December 2024, so the One Big Beautiful Bill Act increase is added back ($750 / $1,500), leaving $15,000 / $30,000 (SCDOR Information Letter #26-4). Bracket edges are derived from the official tax table.

2026.notes: H.4216 (Act 110 of 2026) replaced the old 0% / 3% / 6% schedule from tax year 2026. The new SC Income Adjusted Deduction ($15,000 / $30,000) phases out with income.
